- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., post-85+), often overshooting by 5–10% and failing to correct.
- Shows mean reversion bias: forecasts too low when recent history is high, and too high when recent history is low.
- Lags in response to recent price movements — especially when prices rise sharply, model doesn’t catch the momentum.
- Tends to overcorrect downward after a spike, then undercorrects upward later — creating a “double dip” pattern.
- Forecasts for 30-day horizon are too conservative, especially in high volatility periods — underestimates upward swings.
- When true price rises above 85, model often fails to anticipate the continuation or magnitude of the rise.
- In low volatility periods, model overestimates downward drift — fails to recognize consolidation or sideways movement.
